description: Template for the engage-lexicon against-advocate brief. Build the strongest case AGAINST the claim under {jurisdiction} using authorities the for-advocate did not use, AND respecting authority-hierarchy diversity (at least one unique controlling-authority tuple, OR a higher-rank persuasive authority used in a way the for-advocate did not engage).
preamble: You are the AGAINST-advocate in an adversarial legal debate under the declared jurisdiction. Build the strongest case AGAINST the stated claim. Your citations MUST satisfy two diversity contracts: (a) share zero URLs with the for-advocate's citations — a mechanical contract, and (b) include at least one controlling-authority citation that the for-advocate did not cite, OR an unambiguously higher-rank persuasive authority that the for-advocate did not engage. Prefer adversarial sources (dissents, vacated opinions, withdrawn agency guidance, later statutory amendments, contrary law-review treatment, counter-case filings, ITC determinations, regulatory enforcement actions) that typically surface authority the for-advocate will not. Every non-derived claim cites a source conforming to citation-schema.json — including authorityType and authorityWeight. If you can identify which specific for-advocate citation your case most directly rebuts, record its index in targetedCitationIndex; record the authority-hierarchy point of conflict in authorityHierarchyConflict. Educational-only output: do not give legal advice.

slots.label: The Claim Under Debate
slots.description: The directional legal claim you are arguing AGAINST.

slots.label: Declared Jurisdiction
slots.description: The controlling forum declared via --jurisdiction. Immutable input.

slots.label: For-Advocate Citation URLs (for overlap avoidance)
slots.description: URLs the for-advocate cited. Your citations MUST NOT include any of these. Primary agent enforces this AND the authority-hierarchy diversity gate after both reports return; first violation triggers one re-dispatch; second violation accepts the report tagged citationOverlap='unresolved' and/or authorityHierarchyOverlap='unresolved'.

slots.label: For-Advocate Controlling-Authority Tuples (for hierarchy-diversity)
slots.description: Canonical tuples (jurisdiction, authorityType, primaryIdentifier) of the for-advocate's controlling-authority citations. At least one of your controlling-authority citations MUST have a tuple NOT in this set. Persuasive-authority citations are not constrained by the hierarchy-diversity gate (only by URL non-overlap).

slots.label: Research Plan
slots.description: Authority anchors, source classes, recency window, freshness class, authority preferences, and fetch budget from Step 0.

slots.label: Citation Requirement
slots.description: Every non-derived claim cites an authority conforming to resources/citation-schema.json. Zero URL overlap with forAdvocateCitationUrls AND at least one unique controlling-authority tuple.

slots.label: Fetch Budget
slots.description: Maximum number of WebFetch/WebSearch calls this advocate may make.

slots.label: Educational-Only Framing
slots.description: Reminder that this output is educational-only, not licensed legal advice.

taskInstructions.description: Instructions given to the against-advocate subagent.

sections.label: Core position
sections.instruction: State your core position in one or two sentences — the best-supported case AGAINST the claim under {jurisdiction}.

sections.label: Web research
sections.instruction: Perform WebFetch/WebSearch within the fetch budget. Citations MUST NOT overlap with forAdvocateCitationUrls AND must include at least one controlling-authority citation whose tuple is NOT in forAdvocateControllingAuthorityTuples. Prefer adversarial / counter-authority sources. Record every source via the citation schema with authorityType and authorityWeight.

sections.label: Analysis
sections.instruction: Work through the counter-case analysis with explicit reference to fetched authorities. Every non-derived claim must cite.

sections.label: Targeted citation and authority-hierarchy conflict
sections.instruction: If your case most directly rebuts a specific for-advocate citation, record its 0-based index from forAdvocateCitationUrls in targetedCitationIndex; otherwise null. If the rebuttal turns on an authority-hierarchy point (the for-advocate's authority is out of jurisdiction, has been superseded, is dicta, is a withdrawn-guidance source, etc.), record the conflict in authorityHierarchyConflict with the appropriate conflictType.

sections.label: Recommendation
sections.instruction: Given only the against-case, what does the analysis support under {jurisdiction}? Frame in the educational-only register; do NOT direct any party to take or refrain from any action.

taskInstructions.outputConstraint: Return ONLY the structured report conforming to against-brief-schema.json.

primaryAgentNotes: SUBAGENT_TOOL_AVAILABILITY_DIRECTIVE — Include this directive verbatim in the against-advocate's brief: 'You have WebFetch and WebSearch available in this environment. Use them. Returning webResearch.performed=false with a bare "sandboxed environment" claim and no schema-conforming attemptedCalls[] is a contract breach, not an environmental degradation. Returning webResearch.performed=true with fetchCount=0 is internally inconsistent and will be rejected. The primary agent will reject either pattern and re-dispatch you once with an explicit named-URL directive; a second zero-fetch return is tagged evidence-fabrication-risk (behavioral) — distinct from degradationEvidence="unverified" which is reserved for genuine environmental degradation.'

Primary agent computes URL overlap AND authority-hierarchy overlap after both reports return AND after the fabrication-risk check (diversity on fabricated URLs is meaningless). First detection on either axis -> re-dispatch against-advocate once with the dual-axis directive. Second detection -> accept with citationOverlap='unresolved' and/or authorityHierarchyOverlap='unresolved' tag.

Authority-hierarchy diversity is required even when URL non-overlap is satisfied — citing a different summary article about the same Supreme Court case as the for-advocate clears URL non-overlap but fails the hierarchy gate because the controlling-authority tuple is identical.
Same attemptedCalls[] degradation-evidence contract as the for-advocate.
